## The purpose of this document is to create a clean data set from OPIHI data:

1\) Load libraries

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(readxl)
library(janitor)
library(lubridate)
library(hms)
```

2\) Location for all 20 files

```{r}
excel_files <- list.files(
  path = here("AI_assisted", "AI_data"), #where ever your data folder is located witht the raw files using the here() function
  pattern = "\\.xlsx$|\\.xls$", 
  full.names = TRUE
)
```

3\) Functions

- To read and clean a sheet - filter out chart/ blank sheets (no cell grids)

```{r}
read_single_sheet <- function(file_path, sheet_name) {
  tryCatch({
    # Read sheet as text to prevent column type conflicts during bind
    raw_df <- read_excel(file_path, sheet = sheet_name, col_types = "text")
    
    # Remove completely empty rows and columns
    cleaned_df <- raw_df |> 
      remove_empty(c("rows", "cols"))
    
    # Skip if sheet contains no tabular data (e.g., chart sheet)
    if (nrow(cleaned_df) == 0 || ncol(cleaned_df) == 0) {
      return(NULL)
    }
    
    # Add metadata tracking origin of each row
    cleaned_df |> 
      mutate(
        file_name = basename(file_path),
        sheet_name = as.character(sheet_name),
        .before = 1
      )
  }, error = function(e) {
    # Catches chart sheets or corrupted sheets silently
    return(NULL)
  })
}
```

4\) Iterate on every sheet and file –\> stores all valid tables into a single list

```{r}
# Map through all files and all sheets per file
all_sheets_list <- map(excel_files, function(file) {
  sheets <- excel_sheets(file)
  
  map(sheets, ~read_single_sheet(file, .x)) |> 
    compact() # Drop NULLs (empty/chart sheets)
}) |> 
  list_flatten() 

# Standardize column headers to snake_case across all extracted tables
processed_sheets <- map(all_sheets_list, function(df) {
  df |> 
    clean_names() |> 
    mutate(across(everything(), as.character))
})
```

### \*Remove sheets 3, 48, 50 after manual check\*

- Sheet 3 - Copy of OPIHI field study 2023 - group data sheet

  - not filled out completely + assumption that some cells were filled as an example

- Sheet 48 - OPIHI Field Study 2026 - Waipuilani Data - Quadrat Pt Intercept (Example)

  - Reason: it's an example probably from another data set already in the files

- Sheet 50 - Playing around...Jo March 2022 - just the one sheet

  - Reason: no column names + assumption that data is from OPIHI Data - Reformatted file

```{r}
# Remove multiple sheets b/c unusable)
processed_sheets <- processed_sheets[-c(3, 48, 50)]
```

test - short names

```{r}
# 1. Generate clean list names from file_name and sheet_name inside each data frame
clean_list_names <- map_chr(processed_sheets, function(df) {
  # Extract first row metadata
  f_name <- df$file_name[1]
  s_name <- df$sheet_name[1]
  
  # Remove file extension (.xlsx or .xls)
  f_short <- str_remove(f_name, "\\.(xlsx|xls)$")
  
  # Clean both strings into snake_case and combine
  clean_f <- make_clean_names(f_short)
  clean_s <- make_clean_names(s_name)
  
  paste0(clean_f, "_", clean_s)
})

# 2. Assign the clean names to your list
named_sheets <- set_names(processed_sheets, clean_list_names)

# View all clean names to decide your manual groups
names(named_sheets)
```

test

```{r}
# 1. Define key column terms to detect valid header rows
header_keywords <- c(
  "Date", "Notes", "Location", "latitude", "longitude", 
  "Transect Length", "Num of T", "School"
)

# 2. Helper function to process individual sheets
process_sheet_headers <- function(df, keywords = header_keywords, min_matches = 2, max_scan_rows = 10) {
  
  # Determine how many rows to scan at the top of the sheet
  n_rows_to_check <- min(nrow(df), max_scan_rows)
  if (n_rows_to_check < 1) return(NULL)
  
  # Count unique keyword matches for each row in the scan window
  match_counts <- map_int(seq_len(n_rows_to_check), function(i) {
    row_text <- str_to_lower(paste(df[i, ], collapse = " "))
    sum(map_lgl(keywords, ~ str_detect(row_text, .x)))
  })
  
  best_match_count <- max(match_counts)
  best_row_idx     <- which.max(match_counts)
  
  # RULE: Skip sheet if it fails to match at least 2 keywords
  if (best_match_count < min_matches) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Extract headers from the detected row
  raw_headers <- as.character(df[best_row_idx, ])
  
  # Assign temporary labels to blank header cells so they aren't lost
  raw_headers <- ifelse(
    is.na(raw_headers) | str_trim(raw_headers) == "", 
    paste0("out_of_scope_col_", seq_along(raw_headers)), 
    raw_headers
  )
  
  # Drop all metadata rows above header row, as well as the header row itself
  if (best_row_idx >= nrow(df)) return(NULL) # Skip if no data rows below header
  data_df <- df[(best_row_idx + 1):nrow(df), , drop = FALSE]
  colnames(data_df) <- raw_headers
  
  # Clean names and filter out unwanted columns
  cleaned_df <- data_df %>% 
    clean_names() %>% 
    # Drop sheet_name metadata column
    select(-any_of("sheet_name")) %>% 
    # Remove completely empty rows and columns
    remove_empty(c("rows", "cols")) %>% 
    # Drop columns that fall outside the main data table (blank gaps, artifacts)
    select(-matches("^out_of_scope_col|^x\\d+|^na$|^untitled"))
  
  return(cleaned_df)
}
```

apply

```{r}
# 3. Apply to list of sheet data frames (e.g., named_sheets or a sub-group list)
cleaned_list <- map(reformatted_file, ~ process_sheet_headers(.x, keywords = header_keywords, min_matches = 2))

# 4. Filter out skipped (NULL) sheets
valid_sheets_list <- compact(cleaned_list)

# 5. Combine all valid, cleaned data frames into one master data frame
master_combined_df <- bind_rows(valid_sheets_list)
```

clean

```{r}
# Alternatively, drop any column containing the word "total"
master_combined_df <- master_combined_df %>% 
  select(-contains("excl"))

# 1. Define the key columns that uniquely identify a single field observation
observation_keys <- c("date", "location", "start_time", "stop_time")

# 2. Filter totals, collapse duplicates, and merge unique column values
master_deduplicated <- master_combined_df %>%
  # Drop calculated total columns created in Excel
  select(-matches("(?i)^excl")) %>% 
  
  # Group by the unique observation key
  group_by(across(any_of(observation_keys))) %>% 
  
  # For each column, take the first non-NA value across the matching rows
  summarise(
    across(everything(), ~ ifelse(all(is.na(.x)), NA, na.omit(.x)[1])),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

clean dates and times

```{r}
master_deduplicated <- master_deduplicated %>%
  mutate(
    # 1. Convert Excel serial number to Date (e.g., 2005-04-27)
    date = excel_numeric_to_date(as.numeric(date)),
    
    # 2. Convert fraction of day to HH:MM:SS format
    start_time = as_hms(as.numeric(start_time) * 86400),
    stop_time   = as_hms(as.numeric(stop_time) * 86400)
  )
```

export

```{r}
write_csv(master_deduplicated, here("AI_assisted", "reformatted_clean.csv"))
```
